name: John Newcombe
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Wimbledon singles title at age 23 in 1967 and was ranked the world's top amateur tennis player that year.
early_history_summary: Newcombe played multiple sports as a boy in Sydney before focusing on tennis in his mid-teens. He was Australian junior champion from 1961 to 1963 and joined Australia's Davis Cup team at 19 in 1963. He won his first Grand Slam doubles titles (Australian Championships and Wimbledon) in 1965 at age 20, then broke through in singles with Wimbledon and US Championships titles in 1967.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Newcombe grew up in Sydney and was inspired by earlier Australian tennis champions like Ken Rosewall and Lew Hoad.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian tennis pipeline, Davis Cup, Harry Hopman, junior champion, Tony Roche doubles
evidence_summary: Newcombe was Australian junior champion three consecutive years (1961-1963) and was selected for the Davis Cup team at 19, reflecting the strength of the Australian tennis pipeline under coach Harry Hopman. He won Grand Slam doubles titles with Tony Roche at 20 and singles titles at 23. His early development was shaped by Australia's tennis culture and the Davis Cup system, though family background details are not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Giorgio Parisi
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found. Parisi earned his Laurea in 1970 at age 22 and worked as a researcher at Frascati National Laboratories and visited Columbia University (1973-1974), but his groundbreaking contributions — the Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) equations (1977), the KPZ equation, and the spin glass solution — all came after age 26. His Nobel Prize was awarded in 2021.

name: Candice Bergen
milestone_by_age_26: Made her screen debut in Sidney Lumet's The Group (1966) at age 20 and co-starred in the major studio film The Sand Pebbles (1966) with Steve McQueen, launching a film career that continued through Carnal Knowledge (1971) by age 25.
early_history_summary: Bergen grew up in Beverly Hills as the daughter of famous ventriloquist Edgar Bergen and model Frances Bergen. She began appearing on her father's radio program as a child and was a guest on Groucho Marx's quiz show at age 11. She worked as a Ford fashion model, appearing on the cover of Vogue, before transitioning to acting with her film debut in The Group (1966) while still a college student at the University of Pennsylvania.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Edgar Bergen, one of America's most famous ventriloquists and entertainers, and Frances Bergen, a fashion model. She grew up in Beverly Hills and attended elite schools including Westlake School for Girls and a finishing school in Switzerland.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her father Edgar Bergen was a major radio and film entertainer, and her mother Frances Bergen was a fashion model. Bergen grew up immersed in the entertainment industry, appearing on her father's radio program as a child.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Edgar Bergen daughter, Beverly Hills, Vogue model, Hollywood access, entertainment family
evidence_summary: Bergen's early career was profoundly shaped by her family background: her father Edgar Bergen was one of America's most famous entertainers, and she grew up in Beverly Hills with direct access to Hollywood. She appeared on her father's radio show as a child and was a Vogue cover model before her film debut at 20 in The Group and The Sand Pebbles. Her entry into acting was facilitated by family connections, financial comfort, and geographic proximity to the entertainment industry rather than by formal training or years of practice.

name: Avicii
milestone_by_age_26: Released the single 'Levels' in 2011 at age 22, which became a global hit certified platinum in multiple countries and launched him to international stardom; his debut album True (2013) reached the top 10 in over 15 countries.
early_history_summary: Tim Bergling grew up in Stockholm and started making music at age 16 using a pirated copy of FL Studio, teaching himself production. He posted remixes on electronic music forums and the Laidback Luke forum, adopting the name Avicii. He signed with the label Dejfitts Plays in May 2007 at age 17, remixed tracks for artists like Robyn and Dizzee Rascal, and had a modest European hit with 'Seek Bromance' in 2010 before 'Levels' exploded globally in 2011.
family_context_summary: Mother Anki Lidén was a Swedish actress who appeared in dozens of Swedish films. Father Klas Bergling ran an office supply business. He had three siblings, including an older brother who was also a DJ and proved a pivotal early influence.
parent_family_domain_summary: His mother was an established actress in Swedish film and television, and his half-brother Anton Körberg was an actor. His older brother was a DJ who inspired Tim's early interest in electronic music. The family was middle-class in Stockholm.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Online forums, FL Studio, EDM boom, Stockholm, bedroom producer, Laidback Luke forum, Myspace
evidence_summary: Avicii's rise was driven by early adoption of online music communities (Laidback Luke forum, Myspace) for feedback and distribution, combined with self-taught production skills using FL Studio from age 16. He rode the massive EDM wave of the early 2010s, with 'Levels' (2011) becoming a defining track of the era. His mother's career as an actress and his brother's DJing provided early cultural exposure to performance and music, though his production skills were largely self-developed through online platforms.

name: Bong Joon-ho
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found. By age 26 (September 1995), Bong had made 16mm short films at the Korean Academy of Film Arts, two of which were invited to the Vancouver and Hong Kong international film festivals. However, his feature directorial debut (Barking Dogs Never Bite) did not come until 2000 at age 31, and his major success came later with Memories of Murder (2003) and The Host (2006).

name: Howard Shore
milestone_by_age_26: Was a founding member of the jazz fusion band Lighthouse from 1969 to 1972 (ages 22-25), which released multiple commercially successful albums, and served as music director for the TV program The Hart & Lorne Terrific Hour in 1970.
early_history_summary: Shore grew up in Toronto and began studying music at age 8 or 9, learning multiple instruments and playing in bands by 13. He met Lorne Michaels at summer camp at age 13, forming a lifelong friendship that would shape his career. He studied at the Berklee College of Music in Boston, then became a founding member of the jazz fusion band Lighthouse in 1969, playing saxophone on a half-dozen albums before leaving in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto to a Jewish family. His father Mac Shore was a journalist and his mother Bernice (née Ash) was a dancer. He started studying music around age 8 or 9.
parent_family_domain_summary: His mother was a dancer and his father was a journalist, suggesting an artistic household. He began music studies at age 8-9 and was playing in bands by 13, indicating early family support for musical pursuits.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lorne Michaels friendship, Berklee College, Lighthouse band, Toronto music scene, multi-instrumentalist
evidence_summary: Shore's early career was significantly shaped by his childhood friendship with Lorne Michaels, whom he met at summer camp at age 13 and who later hired him as music director for Saturday Night Live. He studied at Berklee College of Music and became a founding member of the commercially successful jazz fusion band Lighthouse at 22, releasing multiple albums. His mother's background as a dancer suggests an artistic family environment that supported his early music studies.

name: Gianni Infantino
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found. By age 26 (March 1996), Infantino had studied law at the University of Fribourg and served as Secretary General of CIES at the University of Neuchâtel. His career in football administration began at UEFA in August 2000 at age 30, and he became FIFA President in 2016 at age 46.

name: Ivan Lendl
milestone_by_age_26: Was the world No. 1-ranked junior tennis player in 1978 at age 18, winning boys' singles titles at the Italian Open, French Open, and Wimbledon; by age 26 he had won multiple Grand Slam singles titles including the French Open (1984, 1986) and US Open (1985, 1986).
early_history_summary: Lendl was born into a tennis family in Ostrava, Czechoslovakia. His father was a lawyer and former tennis player ranked No. 15 in the country, and his mother was at one point the No. 2 female player. He began playing at age 3, initially hitting a ball against a wall with a paddle. By 14 he could defeat his mother. He dominated junior tennis, winning three boys' Grand Slam titles in 1978 and turning professional that same year, winning seven ATP singles titles by 1980 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Both parents were ranked tennis players in Czechoslovakia. His father Jiří was a lawyer and former player ranked No. 15 nationally, and his mother Olga was once the No. 2 female player in the country. He was an only child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were accomplished tennis players who provided direct domain expertise and coaching from earliest childhood. Lendl began playing at age 3 under his father's guidance and by 14 could defeat his mother, a former No. 2-ranked national player.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tennis family, started at age 3, Czech tennis system, junior Grand Slam titles, Wojtek Fibak mentor, defector
evidence_summary: Lendl's early development was profoundly shaped by being born into a tennis family where both parents were nationally ranked players. He started playing at age 3, received direct coaching from his father, and by his early teens was defeating his mother. This family-domain apprenticeship gave him an enormous head start, leading to junior Grand Slam titles at 18 and seven professional titles by 20. He later benefited from mentor Wojtek Fibak after relocating to the United States, and the experience of defecting from Czechoslovakia added urgency to his career.

name: George Best
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Cup with Manchester United in 1968 at age 22, scoring in the final, and was named European Footballer of the Year; he had already won two English league titles by age 21.
early_history_summary: Best grew up in the Cregagh estate in east Belfast, playing football constantly from a very young age. He was discovered at 15 by Manchester United scout Bob Bishop, who famously telegrammed manager Matt Busby: 'I think I've found you a genius.' Best made his First Division debut at 17 in September 1963, helped United win the league title in 1965 at age 19, and became a global celebrity after scoring twice against Benfica in 1966, earning the nickname 'El Beatle.'
family_context_summary: Born in Belfast to a working-class family. His father Richard 'Dickie' Best was a member of the Orange Order and the family was raised in the Free Presbyterian faith. His mother Anne was an Irish hockey international. Best had five siblings. The family was not wealthy.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football background in the family is documented. His mother was an Irish hockey international, suggesting athletic genes, but there is no evidence of football-specific domain transfer from parents.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Manchester United, Matt Busby, Bob Bishop scout, Belfast, genius talent, European Cup, Denis Law
evidence_summary: Best's rise was driven by extraordinary natural talent recognized by scout Bob Bishop at 15, leading to his signing by Manchester United under Matt Busby. He debuted at 17 and was a league champion by 19, a European Cup winner and European Footballer of the Year by 22. His working-class Belfast background provided little material advantage; his success was built on raw talent, the Manchester United academy pipeline, and the mentorship of Busby and assistant Jimmy Murphy. The scout's telegram — 'I think I've found you a genius' — captures the prodigy-level talent that changed institutional response.

name: Will Smith
milestone_by_age_26: Won the first-ever Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance in 1989 at age 20 for 'Parents Just Don't Understand' with DJ Jazzy Jeff, and launched The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air TV series in 1990 at age 22.
early_history_summary: Smith grew up in a middle-class neighborhood in West Philadelphia. He began rapping at age 12 and met Jeffrey 'DJ Jazzy Jeff' Townes at a house party in 1985 at age 16. They formed the duo DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince, releasing their first single 'Girls Ain't Nothing but Trouble' in 1986 and their first album Rock the House in 1987. 'Parents Just Don't Understand' won the inaugural Grammy for rap in 1989, making Smith famous before he could legally drink. He earned a million dollars before turning 20.
family_context_summary: Born in West Philadelphia to a middle-class family. His mother Caroline was a school board employee and his father Willard C. Smith owned a refrigeration company. He attended Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic School and then Overbrook High School. The family observed the Baptist faith.
parent_family_domain_summary: No entertainment or music background is documented in the family. His mother worked in education and his father owned a refrigeration business. The family was middle-class, providing stability but no industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: DJ Jazzy Jeff partnership, hip-hop wave, Philadelphia, rapping from age 12, Grammy winner, charisma
evidence_summary: Smith's early success was largely self-created, driven by his charisma and rapping skills developed from age 12, combined with a durable partnership with DJ Jazzy Jeff. He rode the wave of hip-hop's mainstream emergence in the late 1980s, winning the first-ever rap Grammy at 20. His middle-class Philadelphia upbringing provided stability but no entertainment industry connections. The partnership with Townes was the key complementary relationship that amplified his natural performative talents.

name: Rod Stewart
milestone_by_age_26: Was the lead vocalist of the Jeff Beck Group, whose debut album Truth (1968) was a hit in both the US and UK at age 23; he joined Faces and released his debut solo album in 1969 at age 24, with his breakthrough album Every Picture Tells a Story arriving in 1971 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Stewart grew up in a working-class family in Highgate, London. He worked various odd jobs including as a fence erector and sign writer before pursuing music. He began busking with a harmonica in 1962 at age 17, joined Jimmy Powell & the Five Dimensions in 1963, then moved through several bands including Steampacket and Shotgun Express before joining the Jeff Beck Group in 1967 at age 22, which included future Rolling Stone Ron Wood. Truth (1968) and Beck-Ola (1969) were both hit albums.
family_context_summary: Born in Highgate, London to a working-class family. His father Robert Stewart was a newsagent and master builder. Stewart worked in the family shop and as a newspaper delivery boy. He was the youngest of five children. The family was of Scottish and English descent.
parent_family_domain_summary: No music background is documented in the family. His father was a newsagent and builder. Stewart's interest in music was self-developed through listening to folk and blues records and busking, not through family connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: London music scene, British blues rock, Jeff Beck Group, busking, working-class, Ron Wood, Steampacket
evidence_summary: Stewart's early career was built through persistence and serial band membership rather than family advantage or formal training. Starting as a busker at 17, he moved through five bands in five years before joining the Jeff Beck Group at 22, where his distinctive raspy voice found a platform on hit albums. His working-class London background provided no industry connections but placed him geographically at the center of the British blues-rock explosion. The partnership with Jeff Beck and Ron Wood was the key complementary relationship that elevated his visibility.

name: Gianni Rivera
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut at age 15 in 1959 (third youngest in history), was bought by AC Milan at 17 for a record transfer fee, won the European Cup with Milan at 19 in 1963, and won the Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year in 1969 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Rivera grew up in Alessandria, Piedmont, where his father was a railway worker. He began playing football with local side ASD Don Bosco and was scouted at 13 by former Milan midfielder Franco Pedroni, who was assistant coach at Alessandria. Rivera made his Serie A debut for Alessandria on 2 June 1959 at age 15 years and 9 months, becoming the third youngest debutant in Serie A history. He scored his first Serie A goal at 16 and was bought by AC Milan in 1960 for a record transfer fee, mentored by Juan Schiaffino. He won the Serie A title with Milan in 1962 and the European Cup in 1963.
family_context_summary: Born in Alessandria, Piedmont, to Edera and Teresio Rivera. His father was a railway worker, indicating a working-class background. Rivera began playing football with local side ASD Don Bosco before being scouted into Alessandria's youth system.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football background is documented in the family. His father was a railway worker. Rivera's football talent was discovered through local youth football, not through family connections to the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Serie A debut at 15, AC Milan, Franco Pedroni scout, Juan Schiaffino mentor, European Cup, Ballon d'Or, Golden Boy
evidence_summary: Rivera's extraordinary early trajectory was driven by prodigy-level talent recognized at 13, leading to a Serie A debut at 15 — the third youngest in history. His father's working-class background as a railway worker provided no football connections; Rivera was discovered through local youth football and scouted by Franco Pedroni. AC Milan bought him at 17 for a record fee, and Juan Schiaffino served as his mentor at Milan. By 19 he was a European Cup winner, and by 26 he won the Ballon d'Or. His path exemplifies how exceptional physical talent, combined with the Italian football pipeline, could propel a working-class teenager to the highest levels of the sport.
